data.description:
LORZOR's Black Friday Gift Picks Feature Leather Wallets He'll Use Every Day

LORZOR's Black Friday Gift Picks Feature Leather Wallets He'll Use Every Day

PR Newswire

LOS ANGELES, CHICAGO and DALLAS, Nov. 27, 2026

LOS ANGELES, CHICAGO and DALLAS, Nov. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- LORZOR is a leather-led brand creating wallets and everyday carry goods for men. For Black Friday 2026, it announces its biggest sale of the year, led by the 1979 leather pop-up wallet series, with up to 62% off selected products and 20% off storewide. Guided by Right in Hand™ philosophy, it brings the warmth of leather and considered engineering to the essentials men carry every day.

For LORZOR, Right in Hand™ means that how a wallet feels matters alongside how it works. Leather texture, weight and proportions are considered together with card access and organization. The brand selects leather for its feel and character, refines designs through prototypes and individually inspects finished products.

THE 1979 SERIES FOR EVERYDAY CARRY

Designed for men who want the familiar feel of leather with quicker card access, the 1979 series incorporates patented design elements into its full-grain leather and aluminum construction. The leather develops a natural patina with use, while a press of the button fans out frequently used cards for easier selection. An anti-jam reset helps release cards if they catch.

CarryLink™ attachment points allow compatible everyday accessories to be connected to the wallet, giving owners more ways to carry what they need. The aluminum cardholder also provides RFID protection for compatible contactless cards stored inside it.

The LORZOR 1979 Wallet suits men who prefer a lighter daily load. Its open layout keeps everyday cards close at hand, while a removable money clip lets them adapt cash carry to the day, keeping essentials together in a compact leather wallet.

The LORZOR 1979 Fold Wallet suits men who want covered storage and easy ID access. A leather cover and magnetic closure keep cards neatly enclosed, an ID window makes identification easy to show, and pop-up access keeps payment cards easy to reach.

Built for those who carry more, the LORZOR 1979 Pro Wallet gives extra cards, identification and cash their own places. Frequently used cards stay ready for pop-up access, while separate storage keeps the rest organized and easier to find. Its magnetic bifold closure gathers these essentials into a compact wallet for work, travel and everyday use.

For shoppers seeking a full-grain leather wallet with AirTag compatibility, the LORZOR TriPop AirTag Wallet adds a dedicated AirTag holder to magnetic trifold storage, pop-up card access and an ID window. With a separately purchased AirTag fitted, owners can use Apple's Find My app to help locate the wallet.

A GIFT HE'LL ACTUALLY USE.

A LORZOR full-grain leather wallet combines thoughtful design with everyday practicality, making it a gift he can actually use. With daily use, the leather develops a natural patina shaped by his touch and travels. Long after the occasion has passed, what began as a gift becomes a familiar part of his life, with a character that is distinctly his.LORZOR's Lifetime Warranty offers added peace of mind, with coverage subject to the warranty terms for each product.

BLACK FRIDAY OFFERS AND SHOPPING INFORMATION

LORZOR's Black Friday 2026 offers include up to 62% off selected products and 20% off storewide with code LZBF2026. Savings vary by product and variant. Current prices and applicable offers are available on the official website.

Shoppers can explore the 1979 series, view the LORZOR TriPop AirTag Wallet and browse LORZOR's Black Friday wallet offers online.

For media inquiries or product samples, contact pr@lorzor.com.

Brand website https://lorzor.com/

data.title: Robbyant Open-Sources LingBot-Map 2.0 and LingBot-Navi, Enabling Long-Term Spatial Memory and Autonomous Navigation for Robots
data.description:
Robbyant Open-Sources LingBot-Map 2.0 and LingBot-Navi, Enabling Long-Term Spatial Memory and Autonomous Navigation for Robots

New models reduce long-distance mapping drift by nearly 85% and reduce the need for redundant exploration across tasks, advancing Robbyant’s universal embodied AI brain.

Robbyant, an embodied AI company within Ant Group, today announced the open-source release of LingBot-Map 2.0, a streaming 3D reconstruction model, and LingBot-Navi, a spatial-memory navigation model. Designed to solve long-distance mapping drift and cross-task amnesia, the models allow robots to build maps on the move, self-calibrate in real time, and navigate complex physical environments with increasing efficiency.

This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261126690702/en/

LingBot-Map 2.0 achieves leading performance in the VBR long-trajectory error test and across nine public benchmark evaluations.

Autonomous mobility is essential for physical AI, from warehouse logistics to last-mile delivery. Yet current systems face two major bottlenecks: long-distance mapping accumulates drift that external correction tools fail to feed back into the model's internal memory, and isolated navigation models force robots to re-explore familiar spaces from scratch for every new task.

LingBot-Map 2.0: Correcting Internal Memory, Not Just Output Trajectories

Building on LingBot-Map 1.0 (released in April 2026), LingBot-Map 2.0 introduces native internal error correction during inference, eliminating the reliance on external place-recognition modules or pose-graph optimization backends.

Powered by Geometric Context Reshaping (GCR), a mechanism inspired by memory reconsolidation in the human brain, the model reuses extracted local geometry and realigns high-level historical memory without re-encoding images. Because GCR updates the model's internal memory layer rather than merely adjusting output trajectories, every correction anchors a reliable spatial reference for future movement. Performance is further bolstered by LingBot-Vision, Robbyant’s visual foundation model, which provides sub-pixel boundary detection to minimize geometric errors at the source.

Key Benchmark Highlights:

  • Real-Time Speed: Achieves 27.51 FPS inference speed on a single NVIDIA RTX 5090 GPU.
  • Near 85% Drift Reduction: In a long-distance VBR urban trajectory test covering 5.2 km and nearly 19,000 frames, the Average Trajectory Error (ATE) dropped from 31.12 meters in version 1.0 to 4.72 meters, a reduction of nearly 85%. This is more than twice as accurate as the best-performing external loop-closure solution (9.98 m).
  • Industry-Leading Accuracy: On the Oxford Spires and KITTI benchmarks, the ATE was reduced to 3.92 meters and 9.42 meters, respectively. Furthermore, the model secured first place across three dense 3D reconstruction benchmarks: CroCoDL, EuRoC, and Oxford.

LingBot-Navi: Accelerating Task Efficiency with Reusable Spatial Memory

Built on LingBot-Map 2.0’s 3D perception, LingBot-Navi introduces persistent spatial memory that carries over between missions. Instead of wiping its map after completing an action, the model retains object and location data, retrieving relevant context when given a natural language command to plan direct routes without redundant exploration.

With every operation, LingBot-Navi refines robots’ understanding of the environment, steadily increasing execution speed. It also supports on-device deployment, keeping user commands and scene data local for low latency and data privacy.

Key Benchmark Highlights:

  • Higher Task Success: In simulations where the model selects targets and navigation is executed by a simulator, LingBot-Navi achieved a 68.60% success rate on the GOAT-Bench subset, outperforming the best of six comparative methods by 10.36 percentage points. In fully end-to-end tests—where the model autonomously plans paths and directly drives movement execution—it reached 56.09% on GOAT-Bench and 32.36% on Robbyant’s proprietary dataset, reconstructed from 36 real-world captured sites.
  • Superior Path Efficiency: Success weighted by Path Length (SPL) measures both whether the robot reaches the target and whether the route is efficient: shorter paths with fewer detours receive higher scores. LingBot-Navi achieved SPL scores of 38.04% on GOAT-Bench and 26.35% on the proprietary evaluation dataset, improving over the best control results by 1.42 and 16.84 percentage points, respectively.
  • Zero-Retraining Gains: Simply upgrading the underlying mapping engine from LingBot-Map 1.0 to 2.0 boosted navigation success rates by 4.15 and 2.35 percentage points across two evaluation sets (with SPL gains of 1.89 and 1.97 percentage points)—proving that higher-precision reconstruction directly improves task completion without retraining the navigation model.

Together, LingBot-Map 2.0 and LingBot-Navi strengthen the capabilities of Robbyant’s universal embodied AI brain — from spatial perception to efficient navigation.

Technical reports, related code, the Pure Streaming model weights for LingBot-Map 2.0, the model weights for LingBot-Navi, and a dataset covering 511 real-world captured scenes are now fully open-sourced to support further community research:

  • LingBot-Map 2.0

Project page: https://technology.robbyant.com/lingbot-map-v2
GitHub: https://github.com/Robbyant/lingbot-map-v2
Hugging Face: https://huggingface.co/collections/robbyant/lingbot-map-v2

  • LingBot-Navi

Project page: https://technology.robbyant.com/lingbot-navi
GitHub: https://github.com/Robbyant/lingbot-navi
Hugging Face: https://huggingface.co/robbyant/lingbot-navi
Dataset: https://huggingface.co/datasets/robbyant/LingBot-Navi

About Robbyant

Robbyant is an embodied intelligence company within Ant Group, dedicated to advancing embodied intelligence through cutting-edge software and hardware technologies. Robbyant independently develops foundational large models for embodied AI and actively explores next-generation intelligent devices, aiming to create robotic companions and caregivers that truly understand and enhance people’s everyday lives and deliver reliable intelligent services across key use cases, such as elderly care, medical assistance, and household tasks.

To learn more about Robbyant, please visit: www.robbyant.com

data.description:
Asian Markets Rise as AI Sentiment Stabilizes

Asian markets tracked gains in U.S. stock futures as sentiment around artificial intelligence stabilized.

----

U.S. Treasury Yields Rise in Shortened Post-Thanksgiving Trade

Treasury yields climbed on Friday as markets reopened for a shortened session following the Thanksgiving holiday.

----

Chinese Shares Lifted as Beijing Signals More Market Support

Authorities reiterated support for capital markets and vowed stabilization policies, amid increased volatility in global markets.

----

Europe Has Picked a New Central Bank Chief. He's in for a Bumpy Ride.

Pablo Hernández de Cos is set to take over from Christine Lagarde at the ECB next year.

----

The AI Boom Looks Alive and Well in Asia

Stocks are having a wild ride thanks to the Nvidia affair, but AI-linked exports and investment are still driving growth-for now.

----

A Game-Changing Move Just Gave America the Edge Over China in AI

Washington closed a loophole that let Chinese companies access Nvidia chips and added overseas cops to curb smuggling.

----

Path for Australian Interest Rates Harder to See

The policy challenges before the Reserve Bank of Australia are growing, and a simultaneous rise in inflation and unemployment has split economists on what the central bank will do next.

----

China's Industrial Profit Surged Despite Headwinds

China's industrial profit surged in October despite mounting domestic headwinds, as robust global demand for its tech products continued to turbocharge exports.

----

OPEC, Allies Face Tough Choices as Surplus Builds, Hormuz Risks Persist

With existing agreements approaching their year-end deadline, the oil cartel faces a difficult balancing act when it meets on Sunday, as the group is set to decide on production targets for 2027.

----

ECB Saw Need for Another Rate Hike Unless Inflation Outlook Improved 'Significantly'

Many officials at the at the central bank viewed another rise in the key interest rate as necessary unless there was a significant cooling of the outlook for inflation, according to an account of their deliberations in October released Thursday.

----

Canada Nonfarm Payrolls Climb in September After Two Months of Declines

Canada's nonfarm payrolls edged upward in September after two consecutive months of decline. The job-vacancy rate also rose for the first time since December.

----

BOE Warns Scale and Breadth Of AI Financing Poses Threat to Financial Stability

The AI investment boom is supporting global economic growth, but the scale and breadth of financing that it requires is making the global financial system more vulnerable to setbacks, the central bank said.

----

New Tariffs on China Risk Undermining Trade Truce With U.S.

China warns it could retaliate if the administration goes ahead with the duties.

----

German Consumer Confidence Edges Up Despite Worries Over Economy, Inflation

Consumer confidence remained at a subdued level amid weak views of the economy and jitters over inflation ahead of the all-important holiday season.
